# Eryri (Snowdonia) National Park: what to see and do

Mountains, castles and coast – there’s plenty of adventure to be found in Eryri, the oldest and biggest of our three National Parks. Here are some highlights of the high country.

SaveShare

## Go for a walk \#1: the quiet ones

Most first-timers want to bag Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon) itself - and fair enough - but there are more than a dozen quieter local peaks that top the magic 3,000ft (914m) figure. They’re all in three neighbouring ranges: the Yr Wyddfa Massif, [Carneddau and Glyderau](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/carneddau-and-glyderau) \- where you’ll find the peak voted British walkers’ favourite, the fabulous [Tryfan](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/wales/carneddau-and-glyderau/walking-and-climbing-on-tryfan). Further south, [Cader Idris](https://www.visitwales.com/things-do/adventure-and-activities/walking/guide-to-walking-up-cader-idris "Cadair Idris walking routes") is a magnificent mountain set around a glacial lake; to the east, the lakeside town of [Bala](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3258) is the starting point for adventures in the Aran and Arenig ranges, where you’re likely to have summits to yourself.

![A man in a yellow jacket standing in the mouth of a cave, looking out over a lake and some mountains](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2021-02/Tryfan__Dan_Struthers.jpg.webp?itok=_pEtqlUb)

## Go for a walk \#2: the easy ones

You can still enjoy the big-mountain experience with small kids, or by wheelchair, or if you simply fancy great views without breaking a sweat. For instance, the circular walk around [Cwm Idwal](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/carneddau-and-glyderau/trails/cwm-idwal-walk) is a relatively easy way to get into the heart of Eryri's most dramatic landscapes, while the [Mawddach Trail](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1979313) (Lôn Mawddach) between Barmouth and Dolgellau has epic views of the estuary and Cader Idris.

Eryri National Park has a good [list of access-for-all walks](https://snowdonia.gov.wales/visit/access-for-all/).

## Go for a walk \#3: the big one

Yr Wyddfa is the highest point in Cymru (and England, for that matter), topping out at 1,085m. On a clear day, the views from the top are astounding, stretching all the way down to Pembrokeshire, up to England’s Peak District and across to Ireland. There are [six routes](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3070/) to the top, and their starting points are all linked by the [Sherpa'r Wyddfa](https://www.gwynedd.llyw.cymru/en/Residents/Parking-roads-and-travel/Travel-passes/Sherpar-Wyddfa.aspx) bus, so you can go up one way and down another. Since 1896 the [Snowdon Mountain Railway](https://www.visitwales.com/product/516165) has chugged up to the summit from late Spring to the end of October.

![Three walkers on the Miner's Track walking towards Snowdon's summit.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2021-01/NVW-C155-1819-0008-small.jpg.webp?itok=NJgBXe5z)

## Have an adventure

[Eryri](https://www.visitwales.com/node/4041/) is the adventure capital of the UK, thanks to the imagination of local entrepreneurs who’ve taken bits of spectacular landscape, and thought, ‘Hmm… what if we did THIS?’ Some of them are wildly improbable, like the world’s fastest zip wires at [Zip World](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1446056), the trippy underground experience of Bounce Below in [Zip World Llechwedd](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1561448), and the 1km-long coaster at [Zip World Betws-y-Coed](https://www.visitwales.com/product/2166718). For these, and many others, check out the local [Adventure Map](https://www.adventuremap.co.uk/).

![Two people on the Zip World Fforest Coaster](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2020-05/NVW-C04-1718-0050-small.jpg.webp?itok=49WrpB2I)

## Go wild and wet

The [National White Water Centre](https://www.visitwales.com/product/926700) offers year-round kayaking and rafting on the River Tryweryn. Strictly speaking, the Menai Strait, which separates Ynys Môn (Anglesey) from the mainland, falls outside the National Park, but it’s an extraordinary stretch of water. It’s a geological fault line, scrubbed out by ice sheets more than 20,000 years ago, and filled by whirlpools and weird tides. It’s a brilliant place to explore by boat, either on a gentle guided tour or – less gently – on the world’s fastest passenger [RibRide](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1225262).

## Visit a castle

Some of the world’s best medieval castles are clustered around the northern fringes of Eryri. The four mightiest - [Beaumaris](https://www.visitwales.com/product/2003622), [Harlech](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1834662), [Caernarfon](https://www.visitwales.com/product/822841) and [Conwy](https://www.visitwales.com/product/527979) – collectively form a UNESCO World Heritage Site. They were built by Edward I (1272–1307) to subjugate the Welsh, but he didn’t entirely succeed in the long run: this remains the most strongly Welsh-speaking part of Cymru, and – sorry, Edward - it’s our red dragon flag that flies over them today. The Welsh princes were pretty handy at military architecture, too. Native Welsh castles are usually smaller than their Norman counterparts, but are always located in spectacularly lovely spots – check out [Dolbadarn](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1014631), [Dolwyddelan](https://www.visitwales.com/product/527773), [Dinas Emrys](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/craflwyn-and-beddgelert/trails/the-legendary-trail-of-dinas-emrys) and [Castell y Bere](https://www.visitwales.com/product/518051). Size isn’t everything, you know.

## Explore our towns

The climbers’ favourite HQ [Betws y Coed](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/north-wales/eryri-snowdonia-mountains-and-coast/outdoor-adventure-activities-betws-y "Outdoor adventure activities in Betws-y-Coed") bills itself as the ‘gateway to Eryri’, while [Beddgelert](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/north-wales/eryri-snowdonia-mountains-and-coast/things-do-kids-family-break-beddgelert "Things to do with kids on a family break to Beddgelert") opts for ‘Eryri's loveliest village’ – and both are hard to argue with. [Blaenau Ffestiniog](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/north-wales/eryri-snowdonia-mountains-and-coast/insiders-guide-blaenau-ffestiniog "An insider's guide to Blaenau Ffestiniog ") sits right in the heart of the National Park but is, weirdly, not actually part of it: its slate-mining moonscape wasn’t considered pretty enough when the boundaries were drawn in 1951. So instead, it’s superbly reinvented itself as adventure central.

Further south, [Dolgellau](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/north-wales/discovering-dolgellau "Discovering Dolgellau") and [Machynlleth](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/mid-wales/powys/must-do-and-around-machynlleth "Must do in and around Machynlleth") are cracking market towns on opposing sides of the Cader Idris massif, while [Abermaw](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5547/) (Barmouth) and [Aberdyfi](https://www.visitsnowdonia.info/aberdyfi) are fine seaside resorts. [Portmeirion](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/north-wales/snowdonia/must-do-and-around-portmeirion "Must do in and around Portmeirion Village") is also a must-visit: the fantasy village was built by architect Clough Williams-Ellis from 1925 to 1973.

## Explore our heritage

Eryri has thousands of years’ worth of human activity to explore, from the Neolithic burial chamber at [Capel Garmon](https://cadw.gov.wales/visit/places-to-visit/capel-garmon-burial-chamber) to the rather more up-to-date hydroelectricity centre at Electric Mountain. In between, there are all those castles we’ve mentioned, the 14th-century [Aberconwy Merchant’s House](https://www.visitwales.com/product/961394), and our [National Slate Museum](https://www.visitwales.com/product/752525). The region’s strong Welsh language heritage is self-evident whenever you step into a shop or pub, but a couple of extra points: the childhood home of the soldier-poet Hedd Wyn, [Yr Ysgwrn](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1970981), has become a shrine to national culture, while [Bala](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/north-wales/snowdonia/bala-breaks "Take a break in Bala, the heart of the Welsh lake district") is a town that’s steeped in Welsh history.

North Wales' history is dominated by the slate industry, and if you want to explore Eryri by foot, there's the wonderful 83 mile circular [Snowdonia Slate Trail](https://www.snowdoniaslatetrail.org/english.html) you can follow using the Snowdonia Slate Trail guidebook / app. The social history and slate landscape is revealed through the remoter towns and villages, disused quarries and lesser-known paths.

## Go for a ride

Cycling has become hugely popular in Cymru, both on and off road: we’ve got plenty of quiet lanes and big climbs, according to the guru of British cycling, Sir Dave Brailsford. He grew up in Eryri, and is honoured with two stunning cycle routes, [The Brailsford Way](https://www.visitsnowdonia.info/ffordd-brailsford-way-cycle-routes-snowdonia), around his old mountain stomping grounds. For MTB riders, [Coed y Brenin](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1971405) was the UK’s first and largest purpose-built singletrack complex, and it’s been joined by several other MTB centres and bases – see [Mountain Bike Wales](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1890240).

## Great little trains

The [Snowdon Mountain Railway](https://www.visitwales.com/product/516165) was purpose-built for tourists in 1896, but the slate industry also left a rather splendid legacy of steam railways that have been re-purposed for fun. And actually, the combined 40 miles (64km) of the [Ffestiniog and Welsh Highland Railways](https://www.visitwales.com/product/517490) make it a practical, as well as stunningly lovely, way to travel around. For these and more, see the our [miniature and narrow gauge railways page](https://www.visitwales.com/inspire-me/days-out/narrow-gauge-and-miniature-railways-wales "The narrow gauge and miniature steam trains of Wales").

## Be safe!

Exploring the outdoors is fantastic fun, but please read up on the risks and make sure you are prepared.

- Follow the [safety advice for exploring Cymru's National Parks](https://www.visitwales.com/info/advice/national-park-safety-information "National Park Safety Information") and these [tips for staying safe on the Welsh coast](https://www.visitwales.com/things-do/nature-and-landscapes/beaches/top-tips-staying-safe-welsh-coast "Top tips for staying safe on the Welsh coast").
- Visit [AdventureSmart.uk](http://www.adventuresmart.uk/) for information on how to stay safe whilst exploring Cymru.

## Frequently asked questions about visiting Eryri National Park

- ### Is Eryri National Park free?











Yes, entry to Eryri National Park is free. However, there may be costs associated with specific activities in the area and for parking or visiting certain attractions within the park.

- ### Can you drive through Eryri National Park?











Yes, you can drive through Eryri National Park. You will encounter some of the most scenic driving routes in the UK, with well-maintained roads that provide access to various areas in the park. Be mindful of the narrow and winding roads, especially in higher areas where you might encounter agricultural vehicles or roaming animals. It's a great way to see the stunning landscapes without having to hike.

- ### What is the closest town to Eryri National Park?











Eryri National Park is surrounded by a number of towns and villages. [Conwy](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3117/) is known for its medieval castle and well-preserved town walls, offering a glimpse into the past. [Caernarfon](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3219/) boasts the majestic Caernarfon Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and a vibrant market town atmosphere. Harlech is famous for its stunning clifftop castle and sweeping views of the coast. [Llandudno](https://www.visitwales.com/node/4282) is a popular seaside resort with a beautiful Victorian pier and promenade. Among the villages, [Llanberis](https://www.visitwales.com/node/6214/) is the gateway to Yr Wyddfa. The village of [Betws-y-Coed](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3568), is perfect for outdoor enthusiasts, and [Beddgelert](https://www.visitwales.com/node/4568/) is a steeped in legend and surrounded by beautiful landscapes.

- ### What is the most picturesque place in Eryri?











There are many to choose from. Llynnau Mymbyr is a breathtaking spot on a clear day. The lake provides stunning reflections of the peaks of Garnedd Ugain and Crib Goch. The dramatic landscape is [Cwm Idwal](https://eryri.gov.wales/walk/cwm-idwal/) \- surrounded by the rugged mountains of Eryri has real wow factor! It’s also steeped in history – Charles Darwin studied geology on the shores of the lake and Sir Edmund Hilary used the area as a practice ground before conquering Everest in the 1950s.

- ### Where can you park at Eryri National Park?











During spring and summer, car parks at Llanberis, Pen y Pass, Nant Peris, and Pont Bethania can get very busy, especially on weekends and during the holidays.



Be mindful of the need to [park responsibly](https://eryri.gov.wales/visit/plan-your-visit/parking-in-snowdonia/) when visiting the area and plan ahead. Only use designated car parks and [Sherpa’r Wyddfa](https://snowdonia.gov.wales/visit/plan-your-visit/snowdon-sherpa/) bus services which operate in the area.



The car park now operates on a pre-booking system. All spaces must be reserved in advance.



The [Eryri National Park website](https://snowdonia.gov.wales/visit/snowdon/parking-for-snowdon/) has information on finding and booking parking spots, including an app providing information on available parking spaces.

- ### Why is Snowdonia now called Eryri?











The official change was made by the park authority in November 2022 and reflects the names traditionally used by Welsh speakers. The aim is to promote the Welsh language, respect the area’s cultural heritage and preserve Welsh heritage for future generations.

- ### What is the hardest walk in Eryri?











[The Watkin Path](https://eryri.gov.wales/walk/watkin-path/) is one of the most challenging routes up Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon), there are some steep sections along this walk and is best suited for experienced hikers.
